purpose: Complete the remaining operator-comparison research rows with full passage context while preserving Level-B status and explicit limits.

project_sequence: House is treated as integrated plurality
persons/nodes can become structural participants rather than isolated units
identity-to-infrastructure language emphasizes relation between distinct parts
biblical_sequence: Christ is named living stone rejected/chosen
believers are also named living stones
they are built into spiritual house
cornerstone and rejection scriptures frame the house
relation_argument.maximum_claim: Useful communal-house analogy. 1 Peter makes Christ the cornerstone and the community the living stones; it does not make one modern individual the entire House.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: The full passage sharpens the project's House metaphor by making plurality non-optional: a living house is constituted from many related stones around a cornerstone, not by collapsing every member into one identity.

project_sequence: central intervention can initiate capability
leadership is judged by whether capability transfers outward
mature systems reduce dependence on one actor by equipping others to act
biblical_sequence: their purpose is equipping the saints
the body is built toward maturity
the larger passage culminates in each part contributing to growth
relation_argument.maximum_claim: Strong structural analogy for leadership that equips others. Ephesians concerns church ministries and Christ's body, not a universal management law.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It gives the project a direct test for healthy central authority: the leader's success is partly visible in whether other members become capable contributors rather than permanent dependents.

project_sequence: ordinary media such as body, object, screen, meme or house can carry meaning
carrier and source are distinguished
the medium's constraints remain even when it mediates something larger
biblical_sequence: divine voice speaks through the encounter
the encounter commissions Moses toward Israel's suffering
relation_argument.maximum_claim: Useful carrier-versus-source analogy. Exodus describes a specific theophany and does not generalize divinity to ordinary media.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: The scene gives the project a disciplined way to talk about symbolic carriers without identifying carrier and source: mediation can be meaningful while the material sign remains bounded and distinct.

project_sequence: Fatherhood is distinguished from biological or legal paternity
relational belonging is treated as potentially symbolic/spiritual
Spirit is modeled as connective relation between source/Father and children/members
biblical_sequence: Spirit-led life is contrasted with flesh/slavery
those led by Spirit are called children
suffering and future glory remain part of the relation
relation_argument.maximum_claim: Useful relational analogy for Fatherhood mediated by Spirit. Romans directs adopted belonging to God in Christ and does not establish a modern human spiritual parentage claim.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: The passage lets the comparator separate biological fatherhood from relational/adoptive Father language while also supplying a strong boundary against transferring Paul's divine-Father role to a modern person.

project_sequence: high authority is linked with protection rather than mere command
vulnerable life is fed and carried
strength is expected to bend toward careful guidance
biblical_sequence: restoration and divine coming are announced
the same figure is immediately pictured as shepherd
relation_argument.maximum_claim: Strong ethical/imagistic comparator for power expressed through care. Isaiah's shepherd is YHWH and does not identify the project with that figure.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: The juxtaposition is valuable because it prevents the project's kingship/height language from being read only as dominance: Isaiah places carrying and gentleness directly beside divine might.

project_sequence: authority is tested through observable treatment of vulnerable people
feeding, welcome, protection and repair are treated as more probative than title alone
ethical outcome becomes a counterweight to grand self-description
biblical_sequence: Son of Man sits in judgment
treatment of the least is interpreted as treatment of the king
correspondences: high judgment tested through low-status encounters
relation_argument.maximum_claim: Strong ethical comparator. Matthew's eschatological judgment does not prove any modern authority claim or provide a generic scoring formula.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: This is one of the clearest biblical tests available for the project's authority language: the scene shifts attention from claimed rank to concrete conduct toward vulnerable people.

project_sequence: healthy correction is framed as developmental rather than punitive for its own sake
formation should increase capability and alignment
later fruit/outcome is used to judge whether correction was healthy
biblical_sequence: discipline is tied to participation in holiness
later peaceful fruit of righteousness is named
straight paths and peace are pursued
correspondences: pain not treated as good in itself
relation_argument.maximum_claim: Useful formation analogy with strong safeguards. Hebrews does not authorize abuse, arbitrary coercion or every claimed correction.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: The full context supplies a practical falsifier for Father/Gardener correction language: discipline cannot be justified merely by calling it discipline; the text itself points toward later fruit, strengthening and peace.

project_sequence: transition to a new state can expose constraints in an old container
some forms must be changed rather than endlessly patched
release from an incompatible box is modeled as part of transition
biblical_sequence: new wine/old wineskins illustrates container failure under new process
correspondences: new process and old container mismatch
relation_argument.maximum_claim: Useful metaphorical comparator for form/content mismatch. Mark's saying addresses Jesus' fasting controversy and is not a universal law of state transitions.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: The context stops the wineskin image from becoming empty innovation rhetoric: 'new container' is warranted by a real mismatch between form and process, not simply by preference for novelty.

project_sequence: observers access a larger structure through limited apertures
different descriptions can arise from different available aspects
model humility is encouraged where access is constrained
biblical_sequence: Moses seeks assurance of divine presence
correspondences: real source with bounded observer access
partial view rather than total possession
relation_argument.maximum_claim: Useful epistemic analogy for constrained access. Exodus does not establish the project's observer geometry or prove that competing modern models share one hidden source.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: This supplies a biblical image for epistemic humility while also limiting overreach: having only a partial view is a reason to qualify claims, not a license to assert the unseen whole with certainty.

project_sequence: source and reflection/interface are distinguished
observers may have real but incomplete models
later integration is expected to revise partial descriptions rather than simply confirm them
biblical_sequence: gift-like abilities are subordinated to love
future fuller knowing is contrasted with present partial knowledge
relation_argument.maximum_claim: Strong humility/partial-knowledge analogy. 1 Corinthians 13 concerns Christian maturity and eschatological fullness, not a technical theory of screens, simulations or hidden geometry.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It makes the comparator itself more rigorous: every Potatoverse/Bible mapping should remain revisable because the passage's own lesson is that present knowledge can be genuine and still incomplete.
